summary.text: Full-term female newborn delivered vaginally at 39 weeks of gestation, birth weight 3,400 g, APGAR 9 at the first minute, to a 35-year-old mother whose pregnancy was poorly monitored (one prenatal visit, no serological screening or prenatal ultrasound, no iron or vitamin supplements).

Initial examination showed a 5 × 1.5 cm umbilical cord hematoma at the fetal insertion with tense dark red to black discoloration; the cord was clamped immediately upon delivery. No malformations, no respiratory distress, no hemodynamic compromise and no resuscitation; cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal and neurological examinations were normal.

Hemoglobin, bilirubin, PT, aPTT and platelet count were normal; the authors state this rules out a primary coagulation disorder as the cause. Monitoring during the first 48 hours was uneventful with progressive improvement of the cord appearance, and the newborn remained clinically stable.
